blocks.raw:
<Tip>
**Memory Aid:** SPT N-value is your soil's report card. N < 10 = soft, weak, lots of settlement (piles!). N = 10–30 = medium, okay for shallow footing with care. N > 30 = strong, dense, shallow footing easy. Compaction is the contractor's promise: "90% Proctor" means 90% as stiff as the lab sample. Clay settles slow (consolidation); sand settles fast (immediate). Know your settlement type or face cracking.
</Tip>

blocks.raw: <WikiMistakeList mistakes={["Assuming SPT N-values are absolute and precise; N-values have ±20% uncertainty and are affected by boring method, hammer efficiency, and soil moisture. Use N-values as estimates, not gospel.","Specifying compaction without verification; many projects specify 90% Proctor but never perform field density tests. Without verification, fill may be 70–80% Proctor, leading to settlement and failure.","Ignoring time-dependent settlement in clay; a building on soft clay may appear stable at 6 months (only immediate settlement has occurred) but crack at 2 years as primary consolidation continues. Monitor long-term.","Confusing bearing capacity with settlement. A soil may have adequate bearing capacity (no shear failure) but unacceptable settlement (foundation drops 100 mm). Both must be checked.","Omitting groundwater effects in bearing capacity; saturated soil has lower effective stress and lower bearing capacity than dry soil at the same SPT N-value. Always consider groundwater level."]} />
